question:
Select the meaning of the given idiom

bring to book
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"bring to book"** means to hold someone accountable for their actions or to punish them. (किसी को दंडित करना)

 
 
• **Example: **The corrupt official was finally ***brought to book*** after years of investigation.
 
 
 
• **"Punish someone" **refers to administering a penalty or sanction on someone for a wrongdoing. **(**किसी को सजा देना**)**
 
 
• **Example: **The judge decided to ***punish*** the thief for his crimes.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer for the given idiom is** to punish someone.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Support someone **(किसी का समर्थन करना): To give assistance or backing to someone.

 
 
• **Example:** She always*** supports ***her friends in times of need.
 
 
 
• **Calm someone** (किसी को शांत करना): To make someone less agitated or anxious.
 
 
• **Example: **The teacher tried to*** calm ***the students during the emergency.
 
 
 
• **Teach someone** (किसी को सिखाना): To impart knowledge or skills to someone.
 
 
• **Example:** He decided to ***teach ***his younger brother how to play the guitar.
